reactions.label: acid-catalyzed tandem Knoevenagel-cyclodehydration xanthene annulation

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one coherent acid-catalyzed cascade rather than a compressed sequence of isolable route nodes: regioselective Knoevenagel condensation joins hydroxybenzaldehyde aldehyde C1 to the less-substituted methylcyclohexanone alpha C5 (product C11=C12); the resulting tether allows intramolecular ortho phenol O9 attack on ketone carbonyl C6 (product O3-C2), followed by dehydration to the fused xanthene. Exact mapping preserves hydroxybenzaldehyde aromatic order 2/3/4/5/7/8 as product 10/9/8/6/5/4, including the pre-existing aromatic fusion edge precursor 8-2 -> product 4-10, and preserves methylcyclohexanone ring order 6/1/2/3/4/5 as product 2/1/15/14/13/12, including pre-existing fusion edge precursor 6-5 -> product 2-12. Hydroxybenzaldehyde para O6 stays product phenol O7; ortho O9 becomes ring O3; aldehyde O0 and ketone O7 leave through two dehydrations. C7H6O3 + C7H12O - 2 H2O = C14H14O2, so every product carbon and retained oxygen is sourced without skeletal rearrangement. p-TsOH is used only as the current-step acid catalyst. The principal unresolved preparative issue is alpha-regioselectivity: condensation must occur at the less hindered CH2 rather than the methyl-bearing CH. That risk lowers confidence to medium but is not an atom-source or topology contradiction. PubChem CID 7213 and 11419 plus Chemical Vendors signals support using the two stable precursors as procurement-oriented leaves, subject to live lot verification.

reactions.rationale: This is one coherent acid-catalyzed cascade rather than a compressed sequence of isolable route nodes: regioselective Knoevenagel condensation joins hydroxybenzaldehyde aldehyde C1 to the less-substituted methylcyclohexanone alpha C5 (product C11=C12); the resulting tether allows intramolecular ortho phenol O9 attack on ketone carbonyl C6 (product O3-C2), followed by dehydration to the fused xanthene. Exact mapping preserves hydroxybenzaldehyde aromatic order 2/3/4/5/7/8 as product 10/9/8/6/5/4, including the pre-existing aromatic fusion edge precursor 8-2 -> product 4-10, and preserves methylcyclohexanone ring order 6/1/2/3/4/5 as product 2/1/15/14/13/12, including pre-existing fusion edge precursor 6-5 -> product 2-12. Hydroxybenzaldehyde para O6 stays product phenol O7; ortho O9 becomes ring O3; aldehyde O0 and ketone O7 leave through two dehydrations. C7H6O3 + C7H12O - 2 H2O = C14H14O2, so every product carbon and retained oxygen is sourced without skeletal rearrangement. p-TsOH is used only as the current-step acid catalyst. The principal unresolved preparative issue is alpha-regioselectivity: condensation must occur at the less hindered CH2 rather than the methyl-bearing CH. That risk lowers confidence to medium but is not an atom-source or topology contradiction. PubChem CID 7213 and 11419 plus Chemical Vendors signals support using the two stable precursors as procurement-oriented leaves, subject to live lot verification.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit the final phenolic O-acryloylation as a real single event: the phenol-bearing advanced chromophore is the route-bearing precursor, and acryloyl chloride supplies the three acrylate carbons and carbonyl oxygen while chloride leaves. Mild tertiary-amine/DMAP-type conditions enable nucleophilic acyl substitution at the phenol; the cationic benzoindolium, thiophene, aryl chloride, and quinazolinone N-H remain structurally unchanged. The canonical audit maps one changed phenolic site, reports same-core preservation and no contradictions; the only inconclusive state is the absence of a forward template and unmodeled base byproducts, which do not undermine product atom sourcing. This late handle installation follows the active hybrid route plan and avoids exposing the acrylate to upstream metal/base operations.

protect_or_preserve: Preserve quinazolinone fused topology and C-Cl through both couplings.
Preserve one boronic acid after the first Suzuki and the thiophene bromide after chromophore formation.

Phenol chromophore -> dye bromide + retained aryl boronic acid (Suzuki).
Retained aryl boronic acid -> 4-bromo quinazolinone + diboronated phenol (mono-Suzuki).
Diboronated phenol -> mono-boron bromophenol -> 2,4-dibromophenol (two mono-Miyaura steps).
preferred_precursor_logic: Use 1-naphthylhydrazine and CC(=O)C(C)C under acid-promoted Fischer conditions to form the benzo[e]indole N-H core; account for C2 methyl an
N-ethylate the isolated N-H core with bromoethane, then condense its activated 2-methyl with 5-bromothiophene-2-carbaldehyde.
Use two independent mono-borylations and one mono-Suzuki before the final acrylation.
protect_or_preserve: Preserve the benzo[e]indole fused naphthalene topology through N-ethylation and condensation.
Preserve one aryl boronic acid after the first quinazolinone Suzuki and the thiophene bromide after chromophore formatio
Preserve phenol and quinazolinone N-H until the final acylation.
mode_evidence: The convergent Suzuki and late O-acrylation events are site-retentive and already validated.
The current benzoindolium N-H scaffold has a chemically credible Fischer indole disconnection: 1-naphthylhydrazine supplies the fused aryl-N
Two staged Miyaura borylations are retained after the multi-site fidelity gate; each edge now changes one aryl site.
N-ethylation and thiophene-aldehyde condensation remain distinct events, preserving the activated 2-methyl donor sequence.
strategic_risks: Fischer indolization must give the correct benzo[e]indolium regioisomer and preserve the C2/C3 substitution pattern.
Hydrazine oxidation/overreaction and protonation/counterion state require controlled acid conditions and isolation.
Mono-borylation and mono-Suzuki selectivity must preserve later handles.
Final acrylation must avoid quinazolinone N-acylation and acrylate polymerization.
revision_triggers: Topology audit cannot prove the new five-membered ring or atom sources from the ketone/hydrazine pair.
Fischer mapping indicates a regioisomer inconsistent with the target C2-methyl/C3,3-dimethyl pattern.
N-ethylation requires a different indolium electronic state or counterion sequence.
Handle preservation fails in either Suzuki.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: Positive chemical case: acid-promoted Fischer indolization of 1-naphthylhydrazine with 3-methyl-2-butanone (pinacolone isomer CC(=O)C(C)C) forms the fused five-membered benzo[e]indole ring and the current 2,3,3-trimethyl N-H cationic electronic state after protonation. The ketone carbonyl carbon becomes C2 and carries the methyl substituent; the alpha carbon becomes C3 and carries the two methyl substituents; the hydrazine aryl-N framework supplies the ring N and fused naphthalene. The event forms the new C-C bond between the ketone alpha carbon and the activated ortho naphthalene carbon, forms the N-C ring bond, expels ammonia/water, and preserves the fused naphthalene anchors. No alternative ring atoms are invented.

reactions.rationale: Commit the Fischer indolization as an intentional scaffold-assembly event with explicit topology override. 1-Naphthylhydrazine and 3-methyl-2-butanone are complete closed-shell precursors: the hydrazine aryl-N framework supplies the benzo[e] fused system and ring nitrogen, while the ketone carbonyl carbon supplies C2 and its methyl substituent and the alpha isopropyl carbon supplies C3 with two methyl groups. Hydrazone formation, acid-promoted [3,3]-rearrangement, intramolecular ortho attack, N-N cleavage, and dehydration/protonation produce the observed five-membered benzoindolium N-H ring. The declared new N-C and C-C ring bonds, preserved naphthalene anchors, and atom-source map directly address both topology proof obligations. Rachel observed one formed and one cleaved heavy bond plus the expected ring-system merge, with no independent contradiction; the missing forward template is a tool limit. The resulting N-H cation is immediately usable for the separately committed N-ethylation.

reactions.label: Ullmann N Arylation

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit the single-event aryl hydrazine formation from 1-bromonaphthalene and hydrazine. The aryl C(sp2)-Br site is the only mapped bond change; hydrazine supplies both product nitrogens and the N-N bond, while the naphthalene carbon framework is retained. A Cu(I)/ligand/base Ullmann N-arylation with excess hydrazine is a chemically established way to install an arylhydrazine on an unactivated aryl bromide, with excess hydrazine limiting over-arylation. No new carbon or ring topology is introduced, and the downstream Fischer indolization in the active hybrid plan uses this N-N unit directly. The forward-template target-not-regenerated flag is a tool limitation; the independent mechanism and atom accounting support continuation, with medium confidence and explicit selectivity risk.

reactions.rationale: One acid-promoted dehydrative bis-Friedel-Crafts condensation joins 2,4-difluororesorcinol and 2,4,6-trifluororesorcinol through a formaldehyde methylene. The trifluoro resorcinol has one available aromatic H, and the difluoro resorcinol position activated by both phenols is selected; the product bridge carbon is supplied by formaldehyde. All four phenols and five aryl fluorides in the product precursor are retained for the subsequent intramolecular SNAr/central-ether closure. The event is treated as one real retrosynthetic step with explicit atom sources, site fidelity, preserved scaffold anchors, and compatible handle timing.

The terminal alcohol of mono-TBS-protected diethylene glycol is deprotonated and attacks one primary end of 1,4-dibromobutane by SN2; atoms C14-C17 and retained Br18 come from the dibromobutane, while the complete TBS-protected diethylene-glycol fragment and its two internal ether links are preserved. Using excess 1,4-dibromobutane and controlled base/loading suppresses bis-ether formation, so the second primary bromide remains as the planned late electrophilic handle. The clear sandbox gate has no contradiction or proof obligation; the template target-regeneration limitation is reconciled by exact precursor/product atom accounting and the inspected O13-C14 bond. This supports the route plan's differentiated mono-bromide/terminal-protected polyether logic.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one selective O-silylation event. Diethylene glycol supplies the entire retained C4H10O3 backbone and both terminal oxygens; explicit TBSCl supplies silicon, the tert-butyl group, and both Si-methyl groups, with chloride as the leaving group. A terminal alcohol attacks silicon under base-assisted conditions, while the internal ether and the second terminal OH remain unchanged. Because the two ends of diethylene glycol are symmetry-equivalent, either end gives the same mono-TBS product; one equivalent of TBSCl or excess diethylene glycol controls mono- versus bis-protection. The evidence-complete attempt supplies all mechanism fields requested by Rachel and has no contradiction or proof obligation. Its inconclusive gate is solely forward_template_unavailable, a stated tool-coverage limit, so no validation override is needed. This step moves the route to stable commodity-like diethylene glycol plus standard TBSCl and supports the planned differentiated protected-polyether sequence.

route_plan_brief.route_thesis: Use a hybrid convergent synthesis. Form the final probe by CuAAC of an azidopropyl coumarin amide and propargyl benzocrown ester. Assemble the coumarin acid from julolidine salicylaldehyde/Meldrum acid. Join a prebuilt sodium benzocrown aryl bromide to a late
key_disconnections: Final azide-terminal-alkyne CuAAC.
Amide coupling of coumarin-3-carboxylic acid with 3-azidopropylamine.
Steglich propargyl esterification of receptor acetic acid.
External Suzuki between benzocrown aryl bromide and tetrafluorofluorescein boronic acid.
preferred_precursor_logic: Use TBS-protected 4-bromo-2-iodophenol so C-I is aminated while C-Br is retained for Suzuki.
Build the secondary amino-polyether acid through protected glycine and a differentiated mono-bromide/terminal-protected polyether chain.
Install boronic acid from the corresponding aryl bromide only after tetrafluorofluorescein core assembly.
protect_or_preserve: Preserve aryl Br and terminal alkyl Br through receptor N-arylation; unmask phenol only immediately before macrocyclizat
Preserve four aryl fluorides, both fluorescein phenols, and lactone carbonyl through borylation/Suzuki.
Preserve benzocrown N/O topology and N-CH2CO2H through Suzuki and esterification.
mode_evidence: The target naturally disconnects at final CuAAC, amide, propargyl ester, and one external Suzuki bond.
The fused coumarin is supported by a complete aldehyde/Meldrum atom balance.
The benzocrown can be built from a complete linear phenol/terminal-bromide tether by one high-dilution Williamson closure.
Aryl iodide versus aryl bromide chemoselectivity enables receptor N-arylation without consuming the later Suzuki handle.
strategic_risks: Protect both phenol and carboxylate as needed during receptor N-arylation/chain elaboration.
Keep the terminal primary bromide out of strongly nucleophilic conditions except planned macrocyclization.
Use mild Suzuki conditions to preserve tetrafluorofluorescein phenols/lactone and suppress protodeboronation.
CuAAC remains final to avoid exposing azide/alkyne to Pd and strong base.
revision_triggers: Buchwald-Hartwig consumes aryl bromide instead of aryl iodide or damages the terminal alkyl bromide.
TBS protection is not orthogonal to chain elaboration or macrocycle closure.
Fluorescein core assembly fails regio/topology or loses one of four fluorides.
Suzuki changes the mapped external bond or lactone topology.

reactions.rationale: This is one selective O-silylation event. Diethylene glycol supplies the entire retained C4H10O3 backbone and both terminal oxygens; explicit TBSCl supplies silicon, the tert-butyl group, and both Si-methyl groups, with chloride as the leaving group. A terminal alcohol attacks silicon under base-assisted conditions, while the internal ether and the second terminal OH remain unchanged. Because the two ends of diethylene glycol are symmetry-equivalent, either end gives the same mono-TBS product; one equivalent of TBSCl or excess diethylene glycol controls mono- versus bis-protection. The evidence-complete attempt supplies all mechanism fields requested by Rachel and has no contradiction or proof obligation. Its inconclusive gate is solely forward_template_unavailable, a stated tool-coverage limit, so no validation override is needed. This step moves the route to stable commodity-like diethylene glycol plus standard TBSCl and supports the planned differentiated protected-polyether sequence.

route_plan_brief.route_thesis: 正向顺序采用混合策略：先由明确取代的吡咯/含氮片段汇聚组装不对称 aza-dipyrromethene 配体，继而 BF2 螯合得到稳定 aza-BODIPY 核心，最后在唯一反应性核心甲基位点与 4-二甲氨基苯甲醛作脱水缩合，形成目标 E-苯乙烯基臂。逆向当前先断开 atom20=atom21。
key_disconnections: 首要：断开非环 atom20=atom21；回到 atom19-CH3 的成熟 aza-BODIPY 核心与 4-二甲氨基苯甲醛，正向为脱水缩合
次要：回溯 N31-B32/B32-F33/F34 配位单元至未络合 aza-dipyrromethene 与完整 BF3 类硼氟源，保持为独立事件
深层：aza-dipyrromethene 共轭骨架按真实成环/缩合机制回溯至取代吡咯和含氮羰基等价片段，不压缩多事件
preferred_precursor_logic: 苯乙烯基臂使用稳定、简单的 4-二甲氨基苯甲醛；避免为同一 C=C 预制 Julia 砜或 Peterson 硅烷
首个核心前体保留目标 BF2 配位及全部环拓扑，只将 atom20 恢复为连接 atom19 的甲基
BF2 用完整 BF3 供体与非亲核碱完成，不把 B/F 拆成无来源原子
protect_or_preserve: 首步完全保留三个五元环及 atom7 对两侧吡咯片段的连接拓扑
保留 N31-B32 与两个 B-F 键直到后续专门 BF2 回溯事件
保留对二甲氨基供体；避免强酸导致持续质子化或强亲核条件导致脱硼
mode_evidence: 结构索引显示目标 atom20=atom21 为非环、共轭 C=C，atom20 连成熟 aza-BODIPY 核心 atom19，atom21 连对二甲氨基苯环 atom22
bond:20 的 Smart CAP 骨架提示保留核心甲基与芳基片段，和甲基-醛 Knoevenagel 原子来源一致
成熟核心晚期编辑只改变一个外周位点；更深处仍必须用 scaffold_assembly 解释三个五元含氮环/配体体系的来源
strategic_risks: 不对称 aza 核心汇聚组装的交叉选择性、区域异构体与互变异构表达
piperidine/AcOH 加热缩合时 BF2 螯合体的水解/脱硼风险，需无水、温和催化并监控
核心多个甲基中 atom19 邻位甲基的位点选择性；其他甲基应因电子/位阻差异保持不反应
目标 atom20=atom21 的 E/Z 选择性及延伸共轭体系光氧稳定性
revision_triggers: Knoevenagel sandbox 显示 atom20/21 原子来源或位点映射不保真
后续结构显示缩合必须在未络合配体上进行，迫使 BF2 与烯基臂安装次序交换
BF2 螯合前体无法以闭壳层、原子守恒的一步事件表达
核心环构建验证出现拓扑矛盾或不能控制不对称取代模式

route_plan_brief.route_thesis: 正向顺序采用混合策略：先由明确取代的吡咯/含氮片段汇聚组装不对称 aza-dipyrromethene 配体，继而 BF2 螯合得到稳定 aza-BODIPY 核心，最后在唯一反应性核心甲基位点与 4-二甲氨基苯甲醛作脱水缩合，形成目标 E-苯乙烯基臂。逆向当前先断开 atom20=atom21。
key_disconnections: 首要：断开非环 atom20=atom21；回到 atom19-CH3 的成熟 aza-BODIPY 核心与 4-二甲氨基苯甲醛，正向为脱水缩合
次要：回溯 N31-B32/B32-F33/F34 配位单元至未络合 aza-dipyrromethene 与完整 BF3 类硼氟源，保持为独立事件
深层：aza-dipyrromethene 共轭骨架按真实成环/缩合机制回溯至取代吡咯和含氮羰基等价片段，不压缩多事件
preferred_precursor_logic: 苯乙烯基臂使用稳定、简单的 4-二甲氨基苯甲醛；避免为同一 C=C 预制 Julia 砜或 Peterson 硅烷
首个核心前体保留目标 BF2 配位及全部环拓扑，只将 atom20 恢复为连接 atom19 的甲基
BF2 用完整 BF3 供体与非亲核碱完成，不把 B/F 拆成无来源原子
protect_or_preserve: 首步完全保留三个五元环及 atom7 对两侧吡咯片段的连接拓扑
保留 N31-B32 与两个 B-F 键直到后续专门 BF2 回溯事件
保留对二甲氨基供体；避免强酸导致持续质子化或强亲核条件导致脱硼

reactions.rationale: 机制真实：C13H16N2 单端 aza-dipyrrin 在 meso atom7 保留 C-H，第二枚 2,4-二甲基吡咯在电子丰富的 alpha 碳进攻后，由 DDQ 完成 C-H/C-H 脱氢氧化，形成目标 tripyrrin 的 atom7-atom15 单键；这是一个明确的氧化偶联事件，不是 Paal-Knorr 或压缩成环。位点与拓扑：声明断点为 product atom7-atom15，中央 aza-pyrrole 原子1-6、已存在的 atom7-atom8 外接键、首枚吡咯原子8-13及其甲基均保留；Rachel strict site_fidelity 报告 same_core=true、changed_site_count=1。由于两个吡咯重复单元，MCS atom_mapping 标为 ambiguous，但它没有给出 contradictions 或 proof_obligations；人工逐原子映射确认第二前体 Cc1c[nH]c(C)c1 的 alpha 碳成为 atom15，其余五元环和两个甲基整体进入产物。原子/电子来源：第一前体提供 C13H16N2 单端骨架与 meso C7，第二前体提供 C6H9N 吡咯；总式 C19H25N3 经 DDQ 脱去 2H 得 C19H23N3，DDQ 仅作电子受体。官能团兼容性和选择性：温和酸催化的吡咯电芳取代/氧化捕获需低温、稀释、限量 DDQ，避免多位点聚合；两个 2,4-甲基和预组织 meso 位点使 atom7-atom15 为主连接。列出的 bond:4 imine/Paal-Knorr 模板不能表达非环 meso C-C 偶联，且给出不可信片段。验证限制：forward_template_unavailable、reagent_byproducts_unmodeled 与 MCS ambiguous 都是工具覆盖/重复骨架映射限制；无化学硬矛盾。此步支持 route_plan revision 2。

declared_intent.rationale_summary: One real acid-catalyzed condensation at target bond 6/meso atom7-to-outer-pyrrole atom8: the C7 aldehyde carbon of CC1=CC(C)=NC1C=O is attacked by the alpha carbon of 2,4-dimethylpyrrole, and dehydration forms the conjugated C6=C7 aza-dipyrrin linkage while installing C7-C8. The formyl aza-pyrrole supplies the complete central ring, its two methyl groups, imine N5, and product meso atom7; the second precursor supplies the complete outer pyrrole ring and its two methyl groups, with its alpha carbon becoming atom8. Reactant formulae C7H9NO + C6H9N give C13H16N2 + H2O, so the aldehyde oxygen and the required hydrogens have an explicit water fate. Trifluoroacetic acid is only the proton-transfer/activation medium. Central and outer ring topologies are retained, no protecting group or hidden oxidation is assumed, and the conjugated dipyrrin tautomer is selected by dehydration under anhydrous conditions.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: One real acid-catalyzed condensation at target bond 6/meso atom7-to-outer-pyrrole atom8: the C7 aldehyde carbon of CC1=CC(C)=NC1C=O is attacked by the alpha carbon of 2,4-dimethylpyrrole, and dehydration forms the conjugated C6=C7 aza-dipyrrin linkage while installing C7-C8. The formyl aza-pyrrole supplies the complete central ring, its two methyl groups, imine N5, and product meso atom7; the second precursor supplies the complete outer pyrrole ring and its two methyl groups, with its alpha carbon becoming atom8. Reactant formulae C7H9NO + C6H9N give C13H16N2 + H2O, so the aldehyde oxygen and the required hydrogens have an explicit water fate. Trifluoroacetic acid is only the proton-transfer/activation medium. Central and outer ring topologies are retained, no protecting group or hidden oxidation is assumed, and the conjugated dipyrrin tautomer is selected by dehydration under anhydrous conditions.

reactions.label: Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons olefination

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Mechanistically real one-event HWE olefination at the mapped styryl C=C: base removes the benzylic/propargylic proton from the chromene C13-CH2 phosphonate, addition to the aryl aldehyde gives a beta-hydroxy phosphonate intermediate, and phosphate elimination furnishes the conjugated Ar-CH=CH-C13 alkene. Site/topology audit is strict and mapped: only product atom 13 changes from the precursor C13-CH2P(O)(OEt)2 substituent to the styryl substituent; the dicyano-bearing C15 site, chromene O/fused aryl ring, and aryl bromide remain in place. Atom sources are explicit: the aryl aldehyde carbonyl carbon supplies styryl atom 11, the phosphonate methylene supplies atom 12, and P/OEt/NaH/THF are non-product leaving/base/solvent components. Functional groups are retained without an unrecorded protection event; two nitriles and aryl bromide are compatible with the planned base, while the free phenol is a stated risk because it will be transiently deprotonated. reactions.label: Knoevenagel-Michael chromene annulation

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: One chemically coherent annulation event: acetone enolate Michael addition to o-hydroxybenzylidene malononitrile creates a tether, then intramolecular phenoxide attack and dehydration furnishes the six-membered 2H-chromene. Exact topology audit: product ring atoms are [1,15,14,9,3,2] (acetone-derived C1, retained phenol O15, retained aromatic fusion atoms C14/C9, aldehyde-derived C3, and acetone-derived alpha C2). New bonds are only product [1,15] (acetone carbonyl carbon to retained phenol oxygen) and [2,3] (acetone alpha carbon to aldehyde-derived benzylidene carbon); the benzylidene C3-dicyano center C2 bond, phenol O10-aryl C9 bond, aromatic C9-C14 fusion edge, and both nitrile attachments are preserved anchors. Atom sources are closed-shell and explicit: malononitrile supplies the dicyano center/nitriles, salicylaldehyde supplies the benzene, phenol O, and aldehyde-derived C3, acetone supplies C1/C2 and the methyl substituent, and acetone oxygen is lost as water during dehydration. No unsupported carbene/radical or placeholder is involved, no extra ring is formed, and no stereocenter is created. The listed Wittig/Julia/Peterson/RCM alternatives were rejected because they do not preserve this anchor map or provide the annulation atom sources.

reactions.label: Friedel-Crafts Acylation

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Mechanism: cyclobutanecarbonyl chloride is converted to a cyclobutanoyl acylium equivalent by a controlled anhydrous Lewis acid, then electrophilic aromatic substitution forms the aryl-sp2-C8 to carbonyl-C9 bond and chloride is released. Use a milder FeCl3 protocol or carefully limited low-temperature AlCl3, strictly anhydrous and with rapid quench, to reduce the known acid sensitivity of the dimethyl acetal. H2 supplies the two hydrogens that convert the aromatic tetrazine (C8H7N5) into the mapped non-aromatic 1,2-dihydro cTz (C8H9N5), with the methyl-bearing carbon, 4-pyridyl bond, and pyridine N retained. The intended event is partial reduction of the N-rich ring only; low H2 pressure/short exposure and catalyst control are used to avoid pyridyl hydrogenation or over-reduction. No C/N atom is added, no ring is opened, and no second reduction event is compressed into this step. This electronic-state correction creates the exact free N-H cTz required for the final mapped N-carbamoylation.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit one oxidative ring-construction event. Acetamidrazone CC(N)=NN supplies the methyl-bearing tetrazine carbon plus three ring nitrogens; 4-cyanopyridine N#Cc1ccncc1 supplies the second tetrazine carbon, the nitrile nitrogen, and the attached para-pyridyl ring. This is distinct from the already committed H2 reduction and is required to supply the aromatic precursor. This is one oxidative ring-construction event; the subsequent H2 partial reduction is a separate committed event already selected in the route sketch.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit one selective amide-forming event on the donor branch. 4-Aminobenzyl alcohol Nc1ccc(CO)cc1 attacks phenylacetyl chloride O=C(Cl)Cc1ccccc1 at the aniline N, displacing chloride to give O=C(Cc1ccccc1)Nc1ccc(CO)cc1. The phenylacetyl carbonyl and benzylic phenylacetyl carbon are sourced from the acid chloride; the p-aminobenzyl alcohol contributes the entire aryl-CH2OH fragment. Chemoselectivity is credible because the aniline is the more nucleophilic site under controlled base, while the primary alcohol is retained and is not carried as a chloroformate until the next late activation step. No ring topology or stereocenter changes. The closed-shell precursor set is atom-balanced and Rachel validation is clear with no contradictions/proof obligations; the alternative alt:0 is rejected because [NH]c1... is an unintended one-electron open-shell representation and the gate explicitly requires correction. Route-plan alignment: supports amide-before-chloroformate donor order and preserves the benzyl alcohol handle.

reactions.label: Suzuki Coupling

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: One real Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling at the mapped aryl-pyrazole junction (current fragment bond:10). The first precursor is the enantiopure alpha-amino aryl bromide CNC(=O)[C@@H](N)c1cccc(Br)c1; the second is the intact pyrazole-boronic-acid/piperazine-phthalimide-glutarimide pharmacophore. Pd-catalyzed transmetalation of the pyrazole C-B(OH)2 bond, oxidative addition to aryl C-Br, and reductive elimination form the single biaryl C-C bond. Br and boron/borate leave as byproducts; every product carbon/nitrogen/oxygen is sourced from the two route-bearing precursors. The alpha [C@@H] stereocenter is remote from the coupling and is not broken; pyrazole aromaticity, piperazine connectivity, and imide ring topology are retained. Chemoselectivity is credible with a mild carbonate/phosphate base and a ligand system chosen to tolerate tertiary amines and imides; avoid prolonged high-temperature exposure to limit boronic-acid protodeboronation. The forward-template target miss is a tool-limit (product similarity 0.7128, no contradiction), so the commit rests on the explicit atom/topology/mechanistic audit. I actually reject Negishi (site:bond:10:alt:0) and Kumada (site:bond:10:alt:1) because organozinc/Grignard reagents are less compatible with the imide-rich fragment, Stille (site:bond:10:alt:3) because of tin handling and slower transfer, and Hiyama (site:bond:10:alt:4) because it requires a less activated silane/fluoride regime; Suzuki is the most practical and site-faithful option.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: One real Fmoc deprotection event at the alpha-amino stereocenter. The route-bearing precursor CNC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc21)c1cccc(Br)c1 is the N-Fmoc-protected version of the current free amine; piperidine/DMF or morpholine-mediated base treatment removes the fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl group, releasing the alpha-NH2 without changing the N-methyl amide, aryl bromide, or [C@@H] configuration. The boronic acid is deliberately retained for the next Suzuki event, while the aryl-piperazine, phthalimide, glutarimide, and all ring sizes/topologies are preserved. Rachel strict site-fidelity mapping passed (same_core=true, one changed site, preserved anchor atoms) and found no contradiction; the forward-template gap is a coverage limit. N-regioselectivity is the main chemical risk because pyrazoles can tautomerize, so use the specified [nH] tautomer, mild carbonate base, controlled temperature, dilute conditions, and analytical isolation of the N-isomer; avoid strong alkoxide or excess alkyl halide that could promote alternative N-alkylation or piperazine quaternization. Atom accounting is explicit for every propyl carbon, pyrazole N, boronic acid handle, and leaving bromide.

reactions.label: SNAr N-Nucleophile

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: One real event: SNAr displacement of the activated aryl fluoride by one end of 1,3-propanediamine to form the secondary aryl amine in the nitro-1,2,4-oxadiazole fragment. The aryl carbon and fused oxadiazole/nitro topology come from O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc(F)c2onnc12; the new N and propyl carbon chain come from NCCCN, while F leaves as fluoride. Nitro substitution and the adjacent electron-poor fused N-O heteroaryl system activate the ipso carbon; the two terminal amines of symmetric 1,3-propanediamine are constitutionally equivalent, so no regioambiguity is introduced. The product retains the fused heteroaryl ring, nitro group, and a free primary amine for the later amide coupling; no stereocenter or ring topology is changed. Rachel reported atom balance as balanced and no contradictions. The gate is inconclusive only because the available forward template did not regenerate the target (tool limit); independent SNAr mechanism, leaving-group identity, electronic activation, and atom-source accounting support the event.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: One real event: quaternization of the neutral indolenine imine nitrogen by the primary bromide of BrCCCCCc1cn[nH]n1. The entire 5-carbon tether and azole ring are supplied by the bromide precursor; bromine is the leaving atom and the indolenine N changes from neutral imine to the product indolium [N+]. The fused benzene/cyclohexene ether chromophore, phosphate monoester, aryl bromide, E-alkene, and all substituent positions are preserved; strict site-fidelity mapping found one changed site and same_core=true. Chemoselectivity is credible because the neutral indolenine imine N is the intended strong nucleophile under polar aprotic quaternization conditions, whereas the azole [nH] is retained and reserved for the later explicit bromoacetic-acid N-alkylation (rxn_2). No ring construction, ring opening, stereochemical change, or implicit protecting group occurs. llm_decision.selection_reasoning: One synthetic event: selective O-phosphorylation of the single phenol on the mature neutral brominated chromophore with POCl3, followed by controlled aqueous replacement of the remaining two P-Cl bonds in the same phosphorylation operation. The phenol precursor supplies every carbon, nitrogen, aryl bromine, ring atom, conjugated alkene, and the aryl O bound to phosphorus. O=P(Cl)(Cl)Cl supplies P and the phosphoryl O; two explicit water molecules supply the two terminal hydroxyl oxygens/protons. Atom balance is reported balanced. Strict site-fidelity mapping gives same_core=true and changed_site_count=1, exactly Ar-OH to Ar-O-P(=O)(OH)2, while the indolenine, fused ether/cyclohexene topology, aryl bromide, and E-alkene are preserved. The single phenol is the intended nucleophile; no other alcohol is present and nitrogen centers are not retained phosphorylated sites. No stereocenter or ring topology changes. Thermodynamic dehydration and conjugation favor the drawn E geometry; no stereocenter is created. Cyclohexanone enamine/enolate attacks the activated carbonyl C5 of COC(OC)C(=O)c1cc(O)ccc1O; dehydration forms product C5=C6. The tethered ortho phenol O14 then closes onto cyclohexanone carbonyl C1 and dehydrates to product O12-C11 and C10=C11. Independent RDKit replay in 134_graph_edit_mapping_mol17_annulation.json maps all 20 product atoms exactly once with element identity: aryl-ketoacetal atoms 0/1/2/3/4/5/7/8/9/10/11/12/13/14 map to product 0/1/2/3/4/5/19/18/16/17/15/14/13/12; cyclohexanone 1/2/3/4/5/6 maps to product 11/6/7/8/9/10. The only new cross-fragment bonds are C5=C6 and O12-C11. Product fusion edge 13-19 is preserved precursor aryl edge 13-7, and fusion edge 6-11 is preserved cyclohexanone edge 2-1. Only the two precursor carbonyl oxygens are absent, matching two H2O eliminations; C10H12O5 + C6H10O - 2 H2O = C16H18O4. The CH(OMe)2 group and retained phenol remain positionally unchanged. Piperidine/acetic-acid buffered dry conditions with continuous water removal are intended to preserve the acetal; acetal hydrolysis remains a genuine preparative risk and limits confidence, but there is no atom-source or topology contradiction. The Hetero-Diels-Alder previews are rejected because their unstable diene fragments and one-bond openings do not represent this two-bond annulation.

C8H6O4 + 2 CH4O - H2O = C10H12O5. Dilute p-TsOH with water removal favors aldehyde over ketone acetalization; overacetalization of the ketone is the main chemoselectivity risk.

Azole N-CH2CO2H: N-H azole plus 2-bromoacetic acid.
Indolium N-pentyl: neutral indolenine plus 5-bromopentyl azole made by Appel conversion of the alcohol.
Fluorobenzofurazan: P(III) deoxygenation of fluorobenzofuroxan after oxidative cyclization of 3-fluoro-2-nitroaniline.
preferred_precursor_logic: Use N-H bromoazole and stable potassium TBSO-pentyltrifluoroborate for C-C coupling; avoid organozinc against unprotected azole N-H.
Keep TBAF removal and Appel bromination as separate late events before indolenine quaternization.
Use stable 3-fluoro-2-nitroaniline as the fluorobenzofurazan source with explicit cyclization and deoxygenation.
protect_or_preserve: TBS protection is explicit on the alkyl-trifluoroborate branch; TBAF deprotection remains a separate committed event.
Preserve aryl bromide, azole N-H until N-alkylation, target E-alkene geometry, and mature fused heteroaryl topology.
Preserve fluorobenzofurazan and aryl F after source-stage cyclization/deoxygenation.
mode_evidence: Existing committed validation supports the late acetal hydrolysis, NBS bromination, chromophore condensation, phosphorylation, and linker op
The azole Negishi continuation was aborted for N-H protonolysis; alkyltrifluoroborate Suzuki retains N-H and TBS protection.
Mol9 source inspection closed the fluorobenzofuroxan and fluoronitroaniline atom map without a topology contradiction.
Mol17 structure inspection places CH(OMe)2 on product atom 5 via acetal carbon 2 and maps the aromatic fusion to a 2,5-dihydroxy aryl ketone
strategic_risks: Aqueous acetal hydrolysis must avoid prolonged acid exposure to the fused aryl ether.
NBS bromination of the phenol can overbrominate; use controlled stoichiometry and temperature.
POCl3 phosphorylation and free-phosphate handling must preserve chromophore integrity.
Azole Suzuki must retain TBS ether and azole N-H.
revision_triggers: A true C/N/halogen or site-fidelity contradiction appears in a committed branch.
Acetal hydrolysis, NBS bromination, or phosphorylation cannot preserve the required scaffold and handles.
Benzofuroxan deoxygenation or nitroaniline cyclization changes aryl-F position or fused N-N-O topology.
Independent atom mapping fails to preserve the mol17 aryl, cyclohexanone, or acetal anchors.

Rachel strict site fidelity finds same_core=true with exactly one changed site, [*]C(=O)C=O to [*]C(=O)C(OC)OC, while both phenolic sites are preserved. Dilute p-TsOH and active water removal favor the aldehyde over the aryl ketone; ketone overacetalization is the explicit chemoselectivity risk. The acetyl methyl carbon remains the product aldehyde carbon, SeO2 supplies its oxygen, and water is a workup reagent; the adjacent aryl ketone C=O, both phenols, aromatic atom order, and the aryl-acyl C-C bond are unchanged. Rachel strict site fidelity reports same_core=true and exactly one changed site, [*]C(C)=O to [*]C(=O)C=O, with both phenolic sites preserved. The inconclusive gate contains no contradiction or proof obligation and reflects unavailable forward-template execution plus the expected unmodeled reduced-selenium byproduct. Free 2,5-dihydroxy substitution creates a real competitive quinone-oxidation risk, so stoichiometry, temperature, oxygen exclusion, and rapid workup must be controlled. The explored primary-alcohol precursor is not selected because it is an additional advanced alpha-hydroxyketone and does not shorten the source route relative to direct methyl-ketone oxidation.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit one real event: intermolecular Buchwald-Hartwig N-arylation of the secondary bridgehead N21 in Nc1nnc(-c2ccccc2O)cc1N1CC2CCC1CN2 with the aryl bromide Brc1ccnc(C#CCN2CCCCCC2)c1. Mechanistically, Pd(0) oxidative addition occurs at pyridine C22-Br, N21 is deprotonated/coordinates, and reductive elimination forms C22-N21; N14 is already tertiary and cannot undergo the same N-H event, while the exocyclic N0 is an aniline-like primary amino substituent whose coordination/competition is the acknowledged chemoselectivity risk. The C22 carbon and all retained heteroaryl/alkyne/piperidine atoms come from the two route-bearing precursors; Br leaves and no new ring atoms or small carbon fragments are hidden. The strict site audit maps exactly one changed site at N21 and preserves N14, the bridged ring bonds, both stereocenters (inherited), the pyridazine/phenol fragment, and the pyridine-alkyne-piperidine topology. The free phenol and primary amino groups are not transformed; use bulky biaryl-phosphine Pd, controlled alkoxide/inorganic base, dilute anhydrous aromatic solvent and temperature screening to favor N21, with protection as a separate route node only if experiments show necessary. The inconclusive gate reflects missing forward-template coverage, not a contradiction; independent atom balance is balanced and no topology/site contradiction was observed. The listed template candidate is not rejected as chemically impossible; this custom action is selected because it records the explicit site/mechanism audit.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: Positive chemical case: with a bulky biaryl phosphine Pd catalyst (for example BrettPhos-class), mild inorganic/alkoxide base, and anhydrous aromatic solvent, oxidative addition of the aryl bromide at pyridine C22 followed by ligand-controlled amination with the only N-H bridgehead (N21) gives the target C22-N21 bond in one real C-N coupling event. The exocyclic aminopyridazine N0 is an aniline-like substituent and is not the intended nucleophile; steric/electronic differentiation plus controlled base favor aliphatic secondary bridgehead N21. Br is the leaving-group atom and is removed; every target C/N atom is sourced from the two listed precursors. The pyridazine-phenol fragment, alkyne-piperidine substituent, bridged-ring bonds, and relative stereochemistry are retained; no ring construction or atom migration occurs. Main risk is catalyst coordination by N0/phenol, which can be addressed by ligand/base/solvent screening or a separate protection step if experimentally required.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit one real event: a dehydrative Knoevenagel condensation of the heteroaryl carbaldehyde with the 2-methyl benzoindolium cation. Mechanistically, mild secondary-amine catalysis generates the uniquely activated C2 methyl nucleophile; addition to the aldehyde followed by dehydration gives the observed trans-styryl bridge. Atom source is explicit: aldehyde carbon is product alkene atom 5, indolium methyl carbon is product alkene atom 6, aldehyde oxygen and two hydrogens leave as water; the independently calculated precursor sum C30H40N7O2+ -> target C30H38N7O+ + H2O. Site and topology are retained: Rachel strict site-fidelity maps one changed heteroaryl substituent site and preserves the fused polyaza and benzoindolium/naphthalene cores, N-propyl, both dimethylamino groups, N-hydroxyethyl, and gem-dimethyl substituents. No ring bond is formed; the reported fused-ring warning is a validator false positive caused by fragment merge/partial MCS coverage, and the new bond is the acyclic exocyclic C=C. Mild base/acetate conditions are chosen to limit cation decomposition and preserve the alcohol; E-selectivity is the intended major geometry from conjugative condensation. Listed Wittig, Julia, and Peterson previews were actually rejected because each preview lacks a complete chemically valid polarity pair for this cationic dye (two aldehyde/placeholder-like fragments or an organometallic donor without a demonstrated source).

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit one real functional-group event: selective SeO2 oxidation of the sole heteroaryl methyl substituent to the planned carbaldehyde. The methyl carbon remains the aldehyde carbon; the added oxygen is sourced from explicit SeO2, while hydrogen abstraction and selenium ester/fragment turnover account for the C-H oxidation. Rachel strict site-fidelity maps exactly one changed site from [*]C to [*]C=O and preserves the fused polyaza core, N-propyl chain, both N,N-dimethylamino groups, ring topology, and all other handles. There is no ring opening, closure, or rearrangement. A single exposed methyl makes site selectivity favorable; controlled SeO2 loading/temperature and workup are required to suppress oxidation of tertiary amino groups and overoxidation of the aldehyde. The action supports the global plan because it installs the aldehyde electrophile immediately upstream of the final styryl coupling. The remaining inconclusive gate is a missing forward template, and the Se byproduct warning is expected reagent accounting rather than a skeleton contradiction; explicit oxygen donor and mapped site replace that tool gap.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: Positive chemical case: acid-promoted Fischer indole rearrangement of 1-naphthylhydrazine with 3-methyl-2-butanone gives the neutral 2,3,3-trimethylbenzo[e]indole. The naphthyl aryl carbon bearing hydrazine remains bonded to nitrogen; the ketone carbonyl carbon becomes the C2 imine carbon bearing the methyl substituent, and the ketone isopropyl carbon becomes the C3 gem-dimethyl bridgehead. The event forms the N-C(ketone) bond and the ortho-naphthyl-C3 bond, closes only the five-membered indole ring, and expels NH3/H2O; formula accounting is C10H10N2 + C5H10O -> C15H15N + NH3 + H2O. Two naphthalene ring anchors and the retained fused bond are preserved, while the new ring atoms are sourced directly from the hydrazine N and both ketone carbons. Regioselectivity is directed by the single 1-naphthyl hydrazine attachment and the Fischer rearrangement; no stereocenter is created. This is a single coherent cyclization event and produces the exact neutral precursor required for N-alkylation.

reactions.rationale: Commit one real Fischer indole scaffold-assembly event. Acid-promoted hydrazone formation and Fischer rearrangement of 1-naphthylhydrazine with 3-methyl-2-butanone closes the five-membered indole ring fused to the existing naphthalene. Exact atom sources: hydrazine N becomes the product imine N; ketone carbonyl carbon becomes product atom 1 bearing the ketone methyl (atom 0); ketone isopropyl carbon becomes the gem-dimethyl bridgehead (atom 13 with methyls 14/15); the sole ortho naphthyl carbon forms the second new ring bond to that bridgehead. The two new bonds are product 1-2 (N-C2) and 12-13 (ortho-C-C3); naphthalene fusion anchors and all retained aromatic bonds remain unchanged. Formula accounting is explicit: C10H10N2 + C5H10O -> C15H15N + NH3 + H2O. No stereocenter is generated and the trimethyl substitution pattern is fixed by the ketone. Rachel proof_required is addressed by the declared ring/topology evidence; the partial MCS reported one cleavage and low coverage because Fischer rearrangement is not template-mapped, while its ring-delta detection correctly flags the intended five-membered fusion. The forward-template absence and unmodeled small byproducts are tool limits, not contradictions. This event materially improves the route by replacing an advanced benzoindole terminal with simple, stable building blocks.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: Commit one real second SNAr substitution: dimethylamine replaces the remaining C-Br bond on the dibromo fused azaheteroaryl core. The current bond:11 site is the only changed site; dimethylamine provides the second NMe2 nitrogen and both methyl carbons, and Br-/N-H leave as HBr. Strict site fidelity maps [*]Br -> [*]N(C)C at one carbon and preserves the first NMe2 arm, N-propyl chain, methyl oxidation handle, fused bicyclic topology, and all ring positions. The already substituted arm differentiates the remaining bromide and electron-poor ring nitrogens activate displacement; controlled excess dimethylamine favors this site without C-N bond scrambling. No stereocenter or ring topology changes. Atom balance is complete; the only inconclusive state is missing forward-template coverage, which is not chemical disproof. This completes the polyaza core immediately before SeO2 oxidation.

This is one late C-N substitution and completes the core immediately upstream of SeO2 methyl oxidation.

Use a copper-mediated aryl amination regime with controlled hydrazine excess and avoid overarylation.

reactions.rationale: This commit is exactly one ester-saponification event on the preformed methyl-ester dye. Hydroxide attacks the ester carbonyl, the tetrahedral intermediate expels methoxide, and aqueous work-up yields the carboxylic acid. The acyl carbon and the full five-methylene N linker are retained from the precursor; water/hydroxide supplies the acid hydroxyl and methanol is the small-molecule leaving product. Rachel's 100% MCS and strict site-fidelity audit independently show one changed substituent, CO2Me to CO2H, with the indolenine rings and mapped polymethine core preserved. There is no other ester, amide, or stereogenic center in this dye fragment, so this is the sole intended hydrolysis site. The all-E polymethine geometry is not newly set; it must be retained and checked chromatographically/spectroscopically under cold, dark, short, pH-controlled conditions. The only inconclusive finding is an unavailable forward template, not a contradiction or atom-source gap. This preserves the revised route-plan handle timing and exposes the acid only immediately before the final amide coupling.

reactions.label: Asymmetric pentamethine cyanine bis-condensation

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one chemically coherent asymmetric pentamethine dye-forming bis-condensation operation. It does not include either indoleninium quaternization or ester hydrolysis, which are separate tree events. The two C2 methyl carbons of the N-(methoxycarbonylpentyl) and N-methyl indoleninium salts become product P11 and P15; the tetramethoxypropane three-carbon backbone becomes P12-P14. The only new inter-component bonds are acyclic P11-P12 and P14-P15. Rachel structure context independently shows both as non-ring bonds, while both existing indolenine systems remain intact: ester-side N9-C10/C10-C28/C28-C31/C31-C36/C36-N9 and N-methyl-side C16-N17/N17-C19/C16-C25/C25-C24/C24-C19 remain their original ring closures. The N9 ester-side anchor and C28 gem-dimethyl anchor, plus the N17 methyl and C25 gem-dimethyl anchors, retain their substituent identity; the MCS changed-site report instead cross-maps the two homologous indolenines. Mechanistically, acid-unmasking of the acetal gives a C3 dialdehyde equivalent and C2 methyl condensation/dehydration installs the polymethine bridge. The four acetal methoxy substituents account for methanol-derived byproducts. No additional ring is formed, opened, fused, or migrated. The methyl ester survives as a non-nucleophilic handle; product geometry is not assumed, so all-E material requires isolation and analysis. This supports the active route plan and its protected-acid timing.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: One defined three-component polymethine-forming reaction operation: two preformed 2-methylindoleninium salts react with the three-carbon dialdehyde equivalent released from 1,1,3,3-tetramethoxypropane. It is not a compressed sequence: formation of each indoleninium salt and hydrolysis of the methyl ester are separate tree events. Product atoms 11 and 15 derive from the C2 methyls of the N-(methoxycarbonylpentyl) and N-methyl indoleninium salts, respectively; product atoms 12-14 derive from the acetal C3 backbone. New acyclic connections 11-12 and 14-15 create the conjugated bridge, while both fused indolenine ring systems retain their internal bonds and substituents. The target's all-E geometry must be isolated and analytically confirmed because the condensation can form E/Z isomers.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: This is one defined three-component polymethine-forming reaction operation, not a compressed sequence: two preformed 2-methylindoleninium salts undergo the standard acid/dehydration-promoted bis-condensation with 1,1,3,3-tetramethoxypropane. Each indoleninium C2 methyl supplies one terminal carbon of the five-carbon bridge, while the acetal supplies the bridge's three central carbons; its four methoxy groups leave as methanol-derived small molecules under the dehydrating medium. Both indolenine rings, N-methyl and N-(methoxycarbonylpentyl) substituents are retained. The only new scaffold connectivity is the conjugated polymethine bridge between the two preserved ring C2 positions; no ring is opened, fused, or rebuilt. C2 methyl acidity/electrophilicity of the salts localizes condensation, and the ester is non-nucleophilic under these conditions. The target encodes all-E polyene geometry: this reaction can generate geometric isomers, so isolate and verify the all-E product rather than treating the reaction name as stereochemical proof. N-alkylations that made both salts and later ester hydrolysis remain separate real events.

reactions.label: Regioassigned N1 alkylation of 4-bromo-1H-1,2,3-triazole

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This commit records one real base-promoted SN2 N-alkylation, not triazole construction, Boc manipulation, or C-Br coupling. The product structure defines the desired new non-ring bond as C10-N11. The selected precursor Brc1c[nH]nn1 is specifically the tautomer whose [nH] is the product-mapped N11: traversing from retained C13-Br gives C13-Br-C12-N11(H)-N16-N15. It therefore has the correct N atom available for deprotonation and alkylation; the alternative Brc1cn[nH]n1 places H at a different triazole N and represents the competing regioisomeric outcome. K2CO3 removes N11-H and N11 attacks the primary C-Br of the Boc-protected aminopropyl electrophile, with bromide loss, so the electrophile supplies the whole three-carbon chain, secondary amide N, Boc carbonyl, tert-butyl, and both oxygens. The triazole supplies its three nitrogen atoms, C12-H, and the retained C13-Br handle. No ring bond or aromatic topology changes; no stereocenter exists. reactions.label: Appel bromination of N-Boc-3-aminopropan-1-ol

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is exactly one Appel alcohol-to-bromide conversion. The N-Boc-3-aminopropanol supplies all retained carbamate atoms, the protected nitrogen, and all three carbons; CBr4 supplies the terminal bromine. Triphenylphosphine forms phosphine oxide and the excess bromine/solvent are non-product species. The expected oxyphosphonium activation followed by SN2 bromide displacement changes only the terminal C-OH functionality, with 0.9167 product atom mapping coverage and no graph/topology contradiction. The Boc carbamate suppresses nucleophilic intramolecular azetidine formation while the reactive C-Br is installed only after protection. No stereocenter exists, and the retained N-CH2CH2CH2 chain is the exact source for the later N11 triazole alkylation. Monitor elimination, incomplete conversion, and Boc loss by LC/MS/NMR; unavailable forward template and unmodeled phosphine/byproducts are tool limits rather than missing product atoms. This supports the plan's late-handle timing.

selected_attempt.action_label: Install terminal bromide after Boc protection

declared_intent.rationale_summary: One Appel bromination replaces the terminal alcohol oxygen of CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCCO with bromine to form CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCCBr. Triphenylphosphine and carbon tetrabromide activate the primary alcohol as an oxyphosphonium species, and bromide performs SN2 displacement at the terminal CH2. The N-Boc-propanol supplies the complete Boc carbamate, nitrogen, and three-carbon skeleton; CBr4 supplies the product bromine; PPh3 becomes phosphine oxide and the remaining bromines leave as non-product salts. The Boc N-C(=O)O, N-CH2, and C-C skeleton are retained; no stereocenter exists. The protected nitrogen is non-nucleophilic under the planned conditions, preventing azetidinium/cyclization pathways associated with an unprotected 3-haloamine. Limit equivalents and verify absence of elimination, dibromination, or Boc loss before the selective triazole N-alkylation.

reactions.label: Selective Boc protection of 3-aminopropan-1-ol

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one selective N-Boc protection event. The MCS map is ambiguous only because the two Boc arms of Boc2O are chemically equivalent, not because the product connectivity is ambiguous. 3-Aminopropan-1-ol contributes the product nitrogen, all three carbons, and the terminal alcohol oxygen; one equivalent Boc arm contributes the installed N-C(=O)O-tert-butyl group, while the other is discarded as CO2/tert-butyl-derived material. The N nucleophile attacks the activated dicarbonate, and its greater nucleophilicity over the alcohol gives the N-carbamate; triethylamine and ethyl acetate are non-product components. The terminal OH is intentionally retained unchanged for rxn_16 Appel bromination, so there is no altered C-C skeleton, ring topology, or stereochemistry. Analyze for competing O-carbonate before proceeding; the ambiguous mapping, absent forward template, and unmodeled base/solvent byproducts are tool/accounting limits with no contradiction or proof obligation. This preserves the route's explicit protection-before-late-halogenation sequence.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: The committed event is one base-mediated diazo transfer at the phenacyl-sulfonium alpha carbon. DBU first forms the resonance-stabilized alpha ylide/enolate-equivalent; nucleophilic capture at p-ABSA sulfur followed by proton transfer and extrusion of p-acetamidobenzenesulfinate gives the alpha-diazo sulfonium cation. The precursor supplies all twelve product carbons except none are newly required, the carbonyl oxygen, sulfur, the two S-methyl groups, the para-ethynylaryl framework, and the alpha carbon; p-ABSA supplies the two nitrogen atoms. Bromide is the counterion carried from the precursor salt and is intentionally absent from the cation-only target SMILES. The validated site-fidelity map reports one alpha-side-chain change and retains the aryl-alkyne scaffold anchor, so neither para substitution nor ring topology changes. The terminal alkyne is not appreciably deprotonated by DBU under a diazo-transfer protocol, whereas the phenacyl-sulfonium CH2 is the acidic, intended site; no stereocenter is created. The unmodeled sulfonyl byproduct and missing forward template are expected tool limits, not atom-source or mechanistic contradictions. The organozinc and organomagnesium template alternatives were rejected because their alpha-diazo-sulfonium carbon nucleophiles would be incompatible with the ketone and cationic diazo functionality.

The C(=O)-C(alpha) bond and para-aryl/alkyne topology are retained. DBU is insufficient to deprotonate the terminal alkyne appreciably, so the designated alpha site is chemoselective. Bromide remains the counterion of the cationic product salt but is omitted from the target cation SMILES/formula.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is a single SN2 quaternization, not a compressed sequence. Dimethyl sulfide attacks the primary alpha-bromomethyl carbon adjacent to the ketone and displaces bromide. The p-ethynylphenacyl bromide preserves every carbon and the ketone oxygen of the route-bearing skeleton; dimethyl sulfide supplies the sulfur plus both methyl groups. The displaced bromide is retained as the counterion of the product salt but is absent from the cation-only current-node SMILES, explaining the nonmodeled bromide warning. Strict site mapping confirms the only scaffold-side change is C(alpha)-Br to C(alpha)-SMe2 and preserves the para-ethynyl aryl anchor. A primary bromide gives SN2 selectivity; dry, neutral conditions avoid alpha elimination, ketone addition, and alkyne reaction. The reacting carbon remains CH2, so there is no stereochemical issue. The template gap is a tool limitation, whereas the mechanism, sources, and site change are independently explicit. The radical thiol-ene and leaving-group-free capping alternatives are chemically rejected as they do not represent this substitution.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: This is one bimolecular SN2 quaternization: neutral dimethyl sulfide attacks the primary carbonyl-alpha bromomethyl carbon of 2-bromo-1-(4-ethynylphenyl)ethan-1-one and bromide departs, furnishing the phenacyl dimethylsulfonium cation. The bromo ketone contributes the full p-ethynylbenzoyl-alpha-carbon skeleton and bromide counterion; dimethyl sulfide contributes sulfur and both methyl groups. The C(=O)-CH2 bond, para aryl substitution, and terminal alkyne remain unchanged; only C(alpha)-Br is replaced by C(alpha)-SMe2. A primary activated bromide supplies the selective electrophilic site, whereas dimethyl sulfide is a soft nucleophile that neither adds persistently to the ketone nor reacts with the terminal alkyne under anhydrous substitution conditions. No stereogenic center is created because the reacting carbon is CH2. The generated bromide is the counterion of the product salt and is omitted from the cation-only node SMILES.

reaction_context.reaction_type: SN2 formation of phenacyl dimethylsulfonium bromide

declared_intent.rationale_summary: This is one bimolecular SN2 quaternization: neutral dimethyl sulfide attacks the primary carbonyl-alpha bromomethyl carbon of 2-bromo-1-(4-ethynylphenyl)ethan-1-one and bromide departs, furnishing the phenacyl dimethylsulfonium cation. The bromo ketone contributes the full p-ethynylbenzoyl-alpha-carbon skeleton and bromide counterion; dimethyl sulfide contributes sulfur and both methyl groups. The C(=O)-CH2 bond, para aryl substitution, and terminal alkyne remain unchanged; only C(alpha)-Br is replaced by C(alpha)-SMe2. A primary activated bromide supplies the selective electrophilic site, whereas dimethyl sulfide is a soft nucleophile that neither adds persistently to the ketone nor reacts with the terminal alkyne under anhydrous substitution conditions. No stereogenic center is created because the reacting carbon is CH2. The generated bromide is the counterion of the product salt and is omitted from the cation-only node SMILES.

reactions.rationale: This is a single SN2 quaternization, not a compressed sequence. Dimethyl sulfide attacks the primary alpha-bromomethyl carbon adjacent to the ketone and displaces bromide. The p-ethynylphenacyl bromide preserves every carbon and the ketone oxygen of the route-bearing skeleton; dimethyl sulfide supplies the sulfur plus both methyl groups. The displaced bromide is retained as the counterion of the product salt but is absent from the cation-only current-node SMILES, explaining the nonmodeled bromide warning. Strict site mapping confirms the only scaffold-side change is C(alpha)-Br to C(alpha)-SMe2 and preserves the para-ethynyl aryl anchor. A primary bromide gives SN2 selectivity; dry, neutral conditions avoid alpha elimination, ketone addition, and alkyne reaction. The reacting carbon remains CH2, so there is no stereochemical issue. The template gap is a tool limitation, whereas the mechanism, sources, and site change are independently explicit. The radical thiol-ene and leaving-group-free capping alternatives are chemically rejected as they do not represent this substitution.

reactions.label: Acid-catalyzed ketone alpha-bromination with NBS

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This commit records exactly one alpha-bromination of the methyl ketone. Under cold, non-radical, acid-catalyzed conditions, 4-ethynylacetophenone enolizes and accepts one electrophilic bromine from NBS; the substrate supplies the entire C10 aryl-ethynyl ketone skeleton and NBS supplies the sole new bromine atom. The alpha hydrogen is removed through enol formation and succinimide is the expected unmodeled reagent byproduct. Site mapping identifies only the methyl-ketone substituent changing to C(=O)CBr and preserves the para-ethynyl aryl anchor, carbonyl connectivity, and aromatic topology. Chemoselectivity is deliberately constrained: no radical initiator, one equivalent NBS, low-temperature addition, immediate quench at ketone consumption, and LC/MS checking for vinyl dibromide or overbromination. In acid the terminal alkyne cannot form an acetylide, while the enol is the kinetic nucleophile. The product alpha carbon is CH2Br, so no stereocenter is introduced. The template gap is a coverage limit, not a contradiction. The thioester/organozinc and aldehyde/dibromomethane local alternatives are chemically inferior and rejected because they rebuild rather than selectively edit the existing ketone and introduce avoidable alkyne incompatibility.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Thioester plus bromomethylzinc reconstruction is less chemoselective and unnecessary for a retained aryl ketone.
Aldehyde/dibromomethane does not provide a credible, selective route to the acetophenone-derived alpha-bromo ketone.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: This is one electrophilic alpha-bromination event. Catalytic p-toluenesulfonic acid forms the enol of 4-ethynylacetophenone; N-bromosuccinimide transfers one bromine atom to that enol to give 2-bromo-1-(4-ethynylphenyl)ethan-1-one and succinimide. The acetophenone supplies the complete aryl, terminal-alkynyl, carbonyl, and alpha-carbon skeleton; NBS supplies the product bromine; one alpha hydrogen is removed in enol formation. The para aryl-alkyne bond, carbonyl C=O, and C(=O)-C(alpha) connectivity are retained, with only C(alpha)-H replaced by C(alpha)-Br. Cold, non-radical, acid-catalyzed conditions favor carbonyl enol bromination; the terminal alkyne is not converted to an acetylide in acid and must be monitored against electrophilic bromination. This risk is controlled by low temperature, one equivalent NBS, immediate quench at ketone consumption, and LC/MS monitoring. No stereocenter is formed at CH2/CHBr2-free alpha carbon in the monobrominated product.

reactions.label: Fluoride-mediated desilylation of TMS alkyne

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This commit is a single fluoride-mediated TMS deprotection. Fluoride attacks silicon, cleavage delivers an aryl acetylide, and water in the same workup protonates it to the target terminal alkyne; trimethylsilyl fluoride and tetrabutylammonium-containing material are expected unmodeled byproducts. The TMS precursor retains the full aryl acetyl ketone and both alkyne carbons, while water supplies the terminal H. The strict map has full target coverage and identifies only the terminal C(sp)-SiMe3 to C(sp)-H edit; it separately preserves the aryl-C(sp) and acetyl substituent anchors, so topology and regiochemistry are unchanged. Buffered, cold exposure controls enolization of the acetyl ketone; no stereocenter is affected. The NBS/acid and later alpha-diazotization are deliberately downstream of this unmasking, while Pd/Cu coupling is upstream. The direct acetylene Sonogashira option is a valid but less operationally controlled alternative; alkynylzinc/magnesium options are rejected for ketone incompatibility.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Alkynylzinc coupling is unnecessary and less compatible with the unprotected acetyl ketone.
Alkynylmagnesium is strongly incompatible with the acetyl ketone.
Direct acetylene coupling is viable but rejected in favor of the safer, protected TMS-alkyne coupling/deprotection sequence.

selected_attempt.action_label: Expose terminal alkyne from TMS precursor

declared_intent.rationale_summary: This is one protecting-group removal event. Fluoride from tetrabutylammonium fluoride attacks silicon in 4-(trimethylsilylethynyl)acetophenone, generating trimethylsilyl fluoride and the aryl acetylide; aqueous workup protonates that acetylide to 4-ethynylacetophenone. The TMS precursor supplies the complete aryl-acetyl-carbonyl and both sp carbons of the product; water supplies the terminal alkyne proton; fluoride removes, rather than contributes to, the trimethylsilyl group. The para aryl-C(sp) bond, aromatic topology, and ketone remain unchanged, with only the terminal C(sp)-SiMe3 substituent converted to C(sp)-H. Buffered, low-temperature fluoride treatment limits ketone enolization or fluoride-mediated side chemistry; no stereochemistry is involved.

reactions.label: Sonogashira coupling of 4-bromoacetophenone with trimethylsilylacetylene

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one Pd/Cu-mediated Sonogashira coupling, with no hidden protection/deprotection or carbonyl conversion. 4-Bromoacetophenone supplies the complete acetophenone aryl fragment and the specific para aryl carbon; trimethylsilylacetylene supplies both newly attached sp carbons and the TMS group. Oxidative addition, copper acetylide transmetalation, and reductive elimination replace the sole aryl C-Br bond with the C(sp)-C(sp2) linkage; bromide leaves into the catalyst/base salt pool. llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one Lewis-acid Friedel-Crafts acylation. Bromobenzene supplies the entire aromatic carbon framework and the bromine retained in the product; acetyl chloride supplies the two acetyl carbons and carbonyl oxygen; AlCl3 generates the acylium-equivalent and is released on hydrolysis. The mapping identifies a single newly installed acetyl substituent on the retained bromobenzene scaffold, while the bromine-bearing scaffold anchor is preserved; no ring bond, carbonyl bond, or stereochemical feature is rewritten. Bromine is ortho/para directing, and the para product is favored sterically but not exclusive. This commit is conditional on isolating analytically pure 4-bromoacetophenone from the ortho isomer by crystallization or chromatography before the Sonogashira event. It does not claim para exclusivity or permit an isomer mixture to enter the route. The lack of terminal alkyne, sulfonium, or diazo functionality makes the AlCl3 operation compatible at the start of the sequence. Partial MCS coverage reflects the two-fragment acylation merger; the acyl atoms have the explicit acetyl-chloride source. Arylzinc/organomagnesium alternatives were rejected because the direct acylium route is simpler and avoids unnecessary organometallic precursors.

reactions.rationale: This is one chemically coherent Knoevenagel event, not an olefination label applied to incompatible precursors. Piperidine generates the resonance-stabilized C-2 methyl carbanion/enamine equivalent of the indolium; addition to the sole aldehyde and dehydration form the target exocyclic C14=C15 bond. The donor aldehyde carbon becomes C14, the indolium 2-methyl carbon becomes C15, and the aldehyde oxygen plus two eliminated hydrogens furnish water; the C16=N17 indolium bond and all remaining heavy atoms are retained. Rachel strict site-fidelity audit maps exactly one donor-core change at product atom 13 (CHO replaced by the target styryl-indolium substituent) and preserves an independent donor-core anchor. The MCS ring-delta text is a fragment-merge artifact: neither precursor ring system is opened, fused, or rewired in the proposed mechanism. The aryl-SMe, oxygen bridge, cyclohexene, gem-dimethyl indolium center, N17-C18 sulfopropyl bond, and sulfonate survive; mild piperidine/acetic acid conditions avoid the strongly acidic, strongly basic, oxidizing, or reducing conditions that threaten the enol-ether-like donor core and thioether. The principal practical risk is E/Z alkene formation, managed by mild buffered conditions, short reaction time, isolation of the E isomer, and 1H NMR/NOE confirmation. The only validation limitation is lack of an executable forward template; there are no contradictions, proof obligations, or evidence gaps, and explicit structural/mechanistic accounting supplies the missing evidence. This supports the revision-1 convergent late-stage assembly plan.

template_evidence.template_name: Pri Alcohol To Aldehyde (Retro, oxidation reduction)

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one real two-electron functional-group interconversion: activated MnO2 selectively oxidizes the exocyclic allylic primary alcohol CH2OH to CHO. The carbon bearing the alcohol is retained as the aldehyde carbon; no C/N/S/O framework atom is introduced into the product, and the oxidant contributes no product atom. Rachel maps the entire scaffold (1.00 product coverage) and observes only the alcohol-to-carbonyl bond-order/functional-group change, with no formed or cleaved bond. All three rings, the oxygen bridge, both C=C bonds, and the aryl methylthio group are unchanged. MnO2 is chosen over strong chromium oxidants, Swern base, or acidic reagents because the substrate has enol/vinyl-ether-like bonds and an oxidizable thioether; neutral, heterogeneous MnO2 oxidation at controlled temperature minimizes hydrolysis, isomerization, and S-oxidation. No stereocenter is created or erased. This preserves the route-plan requirement that the reactive aldehyde be installed late, immediately before the convergent indolium condensation.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one real SN2 sultone-opening event. The neutral indolenine imine N attacks a primary sultone carbon to form product N2-C3, while C3-O9 is cleaved; this accounts exactly for the observed ring-count decrease and ring-bond edit. It does not form or alter a product ring. The N2/C1 iminium unit, fused benzene-indolenine junction C10-C15-C16, and C16 gem-dimethyl substituents are preserved anchors. C3-C5 and S6/O7-O9 all originate from one 1,3-propanesultone molecule, so the target propylsulfonate has no missing carbon, sulfur, or oxygen source; N2 and all indolenine skeletal atoms originate from CC1=Nc2ccccc2C1(C)C. Dry polar aprotic conditions and controlled heat favor the intended primary-carbon SN2 pathway and minimize hydrolytic/exogenous nucleophilic sultone opening. No stereocenter is involved. The forward-template absence is a tool-coverage limitation only; Rachel reports no contradiction, proof obligation, or evidence gap, and the supplied changed bonds, preserved anchors, atom sources, and mechanism reconcile every topology observation. This executes the plan's N17-C18 disconnection and leaves the C-2 methyl intact for the final chromophore condensation.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: One real bimolecular SN2 ring-opening event: the neutral indolenine imine nitrogen attacks a primary methylene of 1,3-propanesultone, forms N2-C3, and cleaves the sultone O-C bond to give the N-(3-sulfonatopropyl) indolium zwitterion. The three carbon side-chain atoms and the SO3 group all come from the intact sultone; N, the C-2 methyl, the benzene ring, and the gem-dimethyl C-3 unit all come from the indolenine. No indolenine C-C, C=N, aryl, or gem-dimethyl connectivity is altered. The primary sultone carbon provides unambiguous regioselectivity; the indolenine nitrogen is the available nucleophile. Conduct under dry polar aprotic conditions with controlled heat, excluding water and external nucleophiles that would competitively open the sultone. This implements the planned N17-C18 disconnection without carrying a less stable 3-halopropanesulfonate reagent.

The terminal hydrazine nitrogen and ketone oxygen account for NH3 and H2O elimination, so no N, O, or carbon is unexplained. This atom map explains the observed fragment merge, ring-count increase, fused system, new junctions, and ring-bond edit. Staged conditions manage hydrazone regioselectivity and avoid acid-driven tar formation; there is no target stereocenter. Imine-only and aza-Wittig previews cannot provide the required C8-C9 annulation or correct ketone substituent source. Imine-only and aza-Wittig previews cannot provide the required C8-C9 annulation or correct ketone substituent source. The unavailable forward template is a coverage limit, with no chemical contradiction/evidence gap; explicit atom-source, retained-anchor, and established mechanism evidence resolves both topology obligations. llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one crossed Claisen-Schmidt condensation/dehydration event. Piperidine forms the enolate at the unsubstituted alpha carbon of 2-(hydroxymethyl)cyclohexanone, which adds to the non-enolizable methylthio salicylaldehyde; beta-hydroxy dehydration forms only the C8=C9 arylidene bond. The salicylaldehyde carbonyl carbon becomes C8, the cyclohexanone alpha carbon becomes C9, and the aldehyde oxygen plus an alpha hydrogen leave as H2O. The strict site-fidelity audit maps precisely this one change from CHO to CH=cyclohexanone at the aromatic attachment and preserves both the aryl-SMe and ortho-OH anchors. The intact cyclohexanone C9-C10-C11-C12-C13-C16 ring, its C13-CH2OH handle, and C16=O remain in the correct topology for the subsequent O17-C16 cyclodehydration. No ring is formed or broken; no product atom comes from piperidine/acetic acid. Slow addition and buffered conditions address ketone self-condensation and phenol compatibility. The exocyclic enone may form E/Z isomers; select/characterize the isomer that cyclizes, while not claiming an unencoded target alkene configuration. The detailed target structure has no assigned stereo location; any transient C13 configuration is removed upon the committed next core-closing dehydration. The forward-template absence is only a tool limit; there are no contradictions, proof obligations, or evidence gaps, and atom-source plus strict site audit independently support the commit. This implements the revision-4 donor-core precursor logic.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one LDA-mediated enolate-trapping event: preformed cyclohexanone enolate attacks formaldehyde and protonation gives the alpha-hydroxymethyl ketone. The cyclohexanone alpha carbon is product C6 and formaldehyde supplies both C7 and O8; the C1=O carbonyl and the entire six-membered ring are retained. Rachel maps one changed site only, the new C6-CH2OH substituent, while preserving the carbonyl-core anchor. An achiral enolate gives an unassigned/racemic C6 center; detailed Rachel structure has no assigned configuration, and the route's committed donor-core cyclodehydration converts the corresponding alpha carbon into C13=C16, so no stereochemical information is silently lost. The forward-template absence is only a coverage limit; no contradiction, proof obligation, or evidence gap was found. This supports the revision-5 source logic and leaves simple cyclohexanone/formaldehyde terminal materials.

reactions.label: Reimer-Tiemann ortho formylation of 4-(methylthio)phenol

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one Reimer-Tiemann ortho-formylation event. Hydroxide forms phenoxide and generates dichlorocarbene from CHCl3; capture at a phenolic ortho carbon and hydrolysis gives the salicylaldehyde. The phenol's para-SMe substitution makes the two OH-ortho positions symmetry-equivalent before reaction, so the desired constitution has no competing positional isomer from those two sites. The strict site audit shows exactly one added CHO at the aromatic site and preserves both the C2-SMe and C5-OH anchors. CHCl3 provides the aldehyde carbon C8; aqueous hydroxide/water supplies aldehyde oxygen O9; chlorides and sodium salts are unmodeled but expected byproducts, not missing product atoms. Benzene topology, aryl-SMe oxidation state, and phenolic O are unchanged; no stereochemistry is involved. Strong base and halogenated-reagent handling are genuine operational risks, addressed by temperature/phase-transfer control, limited conversion, and prompt acidification. The forward-template absence is a coverage limit, not chemical disproof; there are no contradictions, proof obligations, or evidence gaps, and explicit atom accounting plus strict site fidelity supports commit. This closes the salicylaldehyde terminal review with a simpler 4-(methylthio)phenol route leaf.

declared_intent.rationale_summary: One Reimer-Tiemann formylation event: aqueous hydroxide converts chloroform into dichlorocarbene, phenoxide captures it at an OH-ortho aryl carbon, and hydrolysis furnishes the aldehyde. The 4-(methylthio)phenol aryl ring, phenolic O, and aryl-SMe are retained; CHCl3 supplies aldehyde carbon C8 and aqueous hydroxide/water supplies the aldehyde oxygen O9, with chloride salts as byproducts. The phenol has para SMe, so its two phenolic-ortho positions are symmetry-equivalent before formylation, giving the one constitutional product required for the downstream salicylaldehyde. Strong base is a real risk, managed by temperature/phase control and prompt acidification; aryl-SMe is retained and no redox reagent is present. No ring topology or stereochemistry changes.

reactions.rationale: This is one Reimer-Tiemann ortho-formylation event. Hydroxide forms phenoxide and generates dichlorocarbene from CHCl3; capture at a phenolic ortho carbon and hydrolysis gives the salicylaldehyde. The phenol's para-SMe substitution makes the two OH-ortho positions symmetry-equivalent before reaction, so the desired constitution has no competing positional isomer from those two sites. The strict site audit shows exactly one added CHO at the aromatic site and preserves both the C2-SMe and C5-OH anchors. CHCl3 provides the aldehyde carbon C8; aqueous hydroxide/water supplies aldehyde oxygen O9; chlorides and sodium salts are unmodeled but expected byproducts, not missing product atoms. Benzene topology, aryl-SMe oxidation state, and phenolic O are unchanged; no stereochemistry is involved. Strong base and halogenated-reagent handling are genuine operational risks, addressed by temperature/phase-transfer control, limited conversion, and prompt acidification. The forward-template absence is a coverage limit, not chemical disproof; there are no contradictions, proof obligations, or evidence gaps, and explicit atom accounting plus strict site fidelity supports commit. This closes the salicylaldehyde terminal review with a simpler 4-(methylthio)phenol route leaf.

llm_decision.selection_reasoning: This is one genuine [3+2] cycloaddition: the aryl nitrile C/N furnish tetrazole C3/N4 and sodium azide furnishes N5-N7; closure of C3-N7 and N4-N5 creates exactly one non-fused aromatic C1N4 ring. The final aqueous protonation supplies only the tetrazole N-H, while Na/Zn/Br are non-product salts, explaining the atom-balance byproduct warning. Strict site fidelity maps only the former nitrile substituent to the tetrazole at the same C2-aryl position; the chroman framework, aryl F, CF3, O-heterocycle, and pre-existing C2=S configuration are unchanged. Zn(II) activation targets the nitrile, not C-F, CF3, ether, or the saturated stereocenter. The template absence is a declared tool limit; it is outweighed by complete atom sourcing, topology audit, and the standard nitrile-azide cycloaddition mechanism. No listed same-site action was chemically rejected: this is the fully specified realization of Rachel's nitrile-to-tetrazole template. It supports the active late-tetrazole route plan.
